Run complete. Final state verified.

## Result: 1 defect found, fixed, verified, committed

**The defect — an invalid `time` value returned 500 instead of 400** (`1849a13`)

```
PATCH /api/crm/work-orders/:id  {"scheduled_time_start":"not-a-time"}  → 500
POST  /api/crm/work-orders      {"scheduled_time_start":"not-a-time"}  → 500
```

Root cause is subtle: Postgres parses a `time` literal permissively — a token it can't read as a time component it tries to read as a **time zone name**. So an invalid time raises `22023` ("time zone \"not-a-time\" not recognized"), *not* the `22007`/`22008` every other datetime type raises, and `22023` was missing from `errorHandler.js`'s `PG_BAD_INPUT_CODES`. That narrowness is why nine prior runs of fuzzing missed it: `"abc"` → 22007, `"25:99"` → 22008 were always handled; only a hyphen/space whose trailing token isn't a real zone hits `22023`.

`work_orders.scheduled_time_start/_end` are the only `time` columns in the schema and both are written straight from the body on **create and update**, so one entry fixed both verbs. Before widening the code set I grepped all 9 `generate_series`/`TO_CHAR` sites — every one uses a constant step, so no server-authored SQL can raise `22023` and nothing gets masked.

Verified both directions: bad → 400 on PATCH and POST (**no row created**, 10→10), valid `13:45` → 200, `""` → NULL (the `emptyToNull` path intact), `"abc"`/`"25:99"` still 400. Build **PASS** (11.95s). Full sweep re-run: **0 5xx**.

## The dimension: scalar column type confusion — now closed

331 requests over 8 PATCH endpoints × 85 whitelisted fields. Run 114 had closed jsonb *containers*; every other pg type was unmeasured. **155 typed-column probes returned zero 2xx** — `numeric`, `int4`, `bool`, `date`, `timestamptz`, `time`, `uuid`, `text[]`, `jsonb` and all five pg enums reject every wrong type. `time` was the only gap.

## Three secondary results

- **A named open lead was stale for 37 runs.** The gotchas carried an automation `tasks.priority` enum bug addressed explicitly to an api-test stage. It was already fixed in `5329a7e` on both sides; I proved `normalizeTaskPriority` **total** — 13/13 inputs including `undefined`/`null`/`""`/`"bogus"`/`42`/`{a:1}` map to a valid label. Closed with proof.
- **The 168 accepted-but-wrong writes are cosmetic, closed by a type argument.** All 168 are `varchar`/`text`; pg coerces the parameter to text on the way *in*, so the value always reads back a string. Run 68's white-screen needed a **jsonb** column where a boolean stays a boolean — no `.replace()` path can break here.
- **`f7bb323` holds** — Run 114's estimates defect re-probed 6/6 → 400, column never moved.

**DB safety: net zero.** All 8 rows restored byte-identical including `updated_at`; no side-table drift; no row created; no screenshots added.

Two process notes worth flagging: s1 had capped on `max_turns` eight consecutive runs, and batching the discovery (one call for env+login+inventory, one for all 12 whitelists, one 331-request harness — ~20 calls total) is what broke that. And the documented cwd-persistence trap bit twice despite being in the gotchas since Run 79.

Artifact at `C:/tmp/api-test-results.txt` and `/tmp/api-test-results.txt` (223 lines, both fresh). Memory updated: resume entry prepended (33 entries, prior runs intact), gotchas amended, MEMORY.md pointer refreshed. Tree clean apart from the pipeline's own untracked `claude-overnight-20260902-s1-api-test.json`, which I left for the checkpoint commit.
